% 10.11.2023 CRL.M.(BAIL) 767/2023 (for suspension of sentence)
1. The appellant/applicant vide the present application under Section 389 read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 seeks suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail during the pendency of the present appeal against the judgement of conviction dated 16.12.2019 and the order on sentence dated 23.12.2019 passed in Sessions Case No.44713/2015 by the learned ASJ-01, North-East, Special Court (POCSO Act), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi whereby the appellant has been, firstly, convicted for the commission of offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 7 years This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:35:41 alongwith a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default of the said payment, simple imprisonment for a period of 6 months, secondly, convicted for the commission of offence punishable under Section 451 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 1 year alongwith a fine of Rs.3,000/-, in default of the said payment, simple imprisonment for a period of 1 month and lastly, convicted for the commission of offence punishable under Section 174A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 2 years alongwith a fine of Rs.5,000/-, in default of the said payment, simple imprisonment for a period of 3 months in FIR No.561/2015 dated 01.09.2015 registered under Sections 376/451/174A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Karawal Nagar, Delhi.
All the sentences were directed to run concurrently and benefit of Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 was extended to the appellant.

5. This Court has heard the learned counsels and perused the documents on record.
6.
As per Nominal Roll, the overall jail conduct of the appellant has This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:35:41 been 'Unsatisfactory' due to a punishment dated 21.11.2021.
However, the jail conduct of the appellant for the past 1 year has been 'Satisfactory' and he has been serving as a 'Langar Sahayak'.
Further, as per the Nominal Roll, as on 18.05.2023, he has already undergone a period of almost 5 years in judicial custody.

7. Without adverting to the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that since the appellant has already undergone almost half of the awarded sentence, i.e. as on 10.11.2023, he has already undergone a period of almost 5 years and since the hearing of the appeal is likely to take further time, in view of the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sonadhar v. State of Chhattisgarh,
2021 SCC OnLine SC 3182 and Saudan Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259 wherein it has been held that in cases other than the ones concerning life sentences, the broad parameter of 50% of the actual sentence undergone can be the basis for grant of bail, this Court deems it a fit case to suspend the sentence of the appellant till the pendency of the appeal.
